label: Argument From Consciousness
description: Why is some carbon-based matter conscious? Materialism (Dennett) calls it an illusion.

label: Argument From Design Of Life
conclusion: DNA's specified complexity implies a mind.
description: Information only comes from minds; random mutation and macro-evolution cannot supply first life; panspermia concedes natural origin fails.

label: Argument From Fine-Tuning
description: Constants on a razor's edge (the gravitational force to 1 part in 10^40, expansion rate, axial tilt, Jupiter).

label: Argument From Free Will
conclusion: Real freedom is impossible under materialism.
description: Molecules in motion (per Provine) afford no genuine human freedom.

label: Argument From Mathematics
conclusion: Mathematical order comes from mind, not matter.
description: Rationality and mathematics do not arise from randomness.

label: Argument From Poor Design
conclusion: Waste and ruin suggest capricious or absent design.
description: Extinction, collision courses, heat death — not the marks of a careful tuner.

label: Argument From Reason
conclusion: Trustworthy reason cannot be mere chemistry.
description: If thoughts are only chemical reactions, we cannot trust them (Darwin's doubt).

label: Cosmological Argument
conclusion: The universe had a beginning, so it had a beginner.
description: From the Big Bang: a beginning implies a beginner; SURGE supplies the evidence.

label: Deism-Theism Gap
conclusion: A designer is not yet a prayer-answering God.
description: Even granting design, the theist still owes virgin birth, resurrection, vicarious redemption.

label: Moral Argument
conclusion: Objective moral values require a moral lawgiver.
description: A prescription needs a prescriber; the standard is God's nature.

label: Morality Without God
description: No moral act is unique to believers; some wicked acts are unique to them; conscience is innate.

label: Religion Poisons Everything
conclusion: Religion is a corrupting totalitarian tyranny.
description: Its eschatology yearns for the world's end; it demands a master-slave submission.

label: Teleological Argument
conclusion: Order and apparent purpose imply a designer.
description: The design argument; contains fine-tuning and design-of-life as sub-arguments.
